key_insight: In 2D glasses under cyclic shear, the cycles-to-failure diverge near the fatigue limit with a power-law exponent close to -1, revealing a dimensionality-dependent fatigue law.
engineering_relevance: The result helps predict lifetime and damage accumulation in thin or effectively two-dimensional amorphous materials subjected to repeated loading.
method: Atomistic simulations of 2D model glasses under cyclic shear deformation
Track fatigue lifetime as strain amplitude approaches the failure threshold
Use isoconfigurational seeded runs to localize soft regions and test variability
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a power-law divergence of failure time near the fatigue limit, with accumulated plasticity measures such as dissipated work and non-affine displacements scaling consistently with failure time.
watch_item: Seeded soft regions fix where failure occurs but do not remove broad scatter in failure times, so lifetime predictions remain stochastic and require ensembles rather than single runs.
paper_title: Fatigue failure in two-dimensional glasses under cyclic shear deformation
